Glossary

The words we use, in plain language

Borewell
A narrow, deep hole drilled into the ground with a pump that lifts groundwater to the surface. Many Bengaluru homes and businesses rely on one.
Water level / metres below ground
How far below the ground surface the water sits. Every level on this site is a depth: a bigger number means the water is further down, which is worse.
Resting level
The water level after the pump has been off for at least 12 hours: the closest we get to the true groundwater level. This is what the weekly forecasts predict.
Pumping-affected level
A reading taken while or just after the pump runs. Pumping pulls the water down near the well, so these readings look deeper than the true groundwater level.
Drawdown
How far the level drops during a pump run.
Recharge
Water soaking back into the ground, mostly from rain. It reaches borewells slowly, over one to four weeks.
Pump session
One run of a pump, from switch-on to switch-off. The data records the water level at the start and end of each session.
Forecast horizon
How far ahead a forecast looks: one week, four weeks, twelve weeks.
Likely range (80%)
The span in which we expect the real level to land. "80% likely" means that when we tested past forecasts, the real level landed inside ranges like this 8 times out of 10.
Average error / typical error
How far off forecasts were. Average error is the mean miss in metres. Typical error is the middle value: half of forecasts were closer than that.
"Assume nothing changes"
The simplest possible forecast: the level stays where it is now. A useful forecast must beat it.
Testing on the past
Pretending it is an earlier date, forecasting with only the data available then, and checking against what really happened. It is the honest way to measure accuracy.
Real pump data
Actual records from 579 Bengaluru borewells, covering 15 days in July 2026.
Synthetic test system
A simulated set of 450 wells where the true groundwater level is known. It lets us check whether a method finds the right answer.
Digital twin
A physics-based simulation of the same 579 wells over a full year, producing data in the company's own format. It stands in for the long real history we are requesting.
Pressure-point well
A well whose pumping lowers the water across the whole area the most, including in its neighbours.
Crack / fracture / lineament
Water under Bengaluru moves through cracks in hard rock. Wells on the same crack can affect each other even far apart. A lineament map is a geological map of likely cracks.
Sensor drift
A sensor whose readings slowly go wrong over time. It looks exactly like a falling water table, so calibration records are needed to catch it.
Pumping test
Switching one well off (or on) for a few hours while logging its neighbours minute by minute. It measures exactly how strongly and how fast they are connected.
Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
